findings.title: SQL kill-switch reported as invalid SQL
findings.body: The legacy expression path still builds a SQLCommand via NewSQLCommand, which calls sql.TablesList. That now always fails because pkg/expr/sql/db.go RunCommands returns "not implemented" after DuckDB was removed. NewSQLCommand maps every such failure to a BadRequest (sql-invalid-sql / "error reading SQL command") and logs "invalid sql query". Previously valid SQL expressions are therefore rejected as malformed user SQL, not as a disabled feature. ExpressionQueryReader is a second entry point and returns a different error, "sqlExpressions is not implemented" (pkg/expr/reader.go), while enableSqlExpressions ignores FlagSqlExpressions and always returns false. Clients and the UI cannot tell a security disable (CVE-2024-9264) from a bad query, and the still-documented feature flag does not change either outcome.

findings.title: No test that SQL expressions stay disabled
findings.body: This change removes the DuckDB engine and is meant to close RCE/LFI via SQL expressions, but it adds no test that a SQL expression is rejected on both entry points (ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery and UnmarshalSQLCommand/Execute) and that no query is executed. The only enforcement on the legacy path is a stub whose errors are labeled "not implemented", and enableSqlExpressions is an inverted flag check that happens to return false on every branch. A regression that fills in the stub or "fixes" that helper would restore execution with no CI failure. The PR description records only manual checks.
